title: Turn project inputs into a Construction Set your designer can review.

Teams with existing project folders, templates and completed jobs that can become a useful evaluation set.

problems.title: The brief is scattered

problems.title: Preparation competes with design
problems.body: Formatting documents, copying selections and matching images take attention away from design decisions. A scoped workflow can prepare these repeatable elements in your format, with the source material available to the reviewer.

problems.title: One change creates another checking job
problems.body: A revised fixture or room selection can affect several parts of a document. We define controlled revisions and version history so the designer can see what changed and check related sections before release.

deliverables.body: A way to request defined changes, retain versions and record review. Client delivery stays behind an explicit approval step. Any requested project-system updates are scoped separately by action and permission.

deliverables.title: A handover your team can use
deliverables.body: Documented inputs, operating instructions, permissions and exception handling, plus a team walkthrough. Hosting, third-party usage and ongoing support are identified in the proposal.

workflow.title: Collect the approved inputs
workflow.body: Read the agreed project folder and selected notes, plans, photographs and product information. Keep the source of each material selection available.

workflow.title: Resolve the brief
workflow.body: Prepare the structured brief and a list of missing or conflicting information. The designer confirms what can move forward.

workflow.title: Prepare and revise the draft
workflow.body: Assemble the agreed document sections and schedule. Apply reviewed changes while retaining the earlier version.

workflow.title: Approve the set
workflow.body: The responsible designer checks the content and any required professional review. An authorized person approves release to the client or project team.

Managing partners and operations leads coordinating documents, deadlines and handoffs across a team.
Practices with a defined monthly process and a reviewer who can help establish what complete means.

problems.title: The client picture is split across tools
problems.body: Email, document storage, practice software and the accounting system each hold part of the story. A scoped operating view can bring agreed status fields together, showing where information came from and when it was last updated.

problems.title: Document chasing repeats every cycle
problems.body: Your team checks the same list, searches for attachments and prepares another request. We define which items are expected, how arrivals are matched and when an exception needs a person rather than another reminder.

problems.title: An exception needs an owner
problems.body: An unresolved question can sit between the client coordinator and the delivery team. The workflow can prepare a task with context, source links and a named owner, then make its review status visible.

deliverables.title: An exception and approval queue
deliverables.body: A place to review conflicting information, unmatched documents and proposed changes. Every write action has a defined destination, permission and approval owner.

deliverables.title: An operating guide and handover
deliverables.body: Documented rules, source mappings, access arrangements and failure handling. Your team learns how to review the queue, correct an item and recognize when a connection needs attention.

workflow.title: Define the expected package
workflow.body: Choose one service and reporting period. Your practice lead defines required documents, responsible staff and the checks that establish completeness.

workflow.title: Match incoming information
workflow.body: Read agreed sources and propose a client, period and document type. Ambiguous matches stay in the review queue.

workflow.title: Prepare the next action
workflow.body: Show what is missing and draft the appropriate request or internal task. Include the source context needed to check it.

workflow.title: Review and record
workflow.body: Your team approves the action. The workflow records the decision and, where explicitly scoped, updates the approved system.

kicker: FOR U.S. REAL ESTATE LEGAL AND TRANSACTION TEAMS
title: Put the evidence beside every property-document finding.
description: Custom document comparison workflows that prepare reviewable findings, source references and open questions for your real estate team.
lead: Property review often means finding the same fact in several documents, checking whether the sources agree and explaining what still needs attention. FutureProof Agents builds a bounded workflow for that preparation: organize the approved documents, compare defined fields and produce a draft with evidence your reviewer can inspect.
audience: Real estate law firms and transaction teams reviewing recurring property document packages.
Practice leads, senior paralegals and operations managers responsible for review quality and turnaround.
Teams able to define one jurisdiction, a clear document family and the qualified person who approves findings.

problems.title: Finding the relevant passage takes work
problems.body: Long files, scans and inconsistent document structures slow down a comparison before professional judgment begins. We define the facts and passages to locate, then keep page references and relevant excerpts attached to the draft findings.

problems.title: Conflicting sources need to stay visible
problems.body: A property identifier, attachment or stated provision may differ across records. The workflow can organize those differences into a review queue. A missing or unclear source remains an open question for the reviewer.

problems.title: A summary needs a traceable foundation
problems.body: A polished paragraph is difficult to check without its evidence. We structure the output so your team can move from a finding to the document and page behind it, then record a correction or approval.

deliverables.title: A scoped document and review checklist
deliverables.body: An agreed jurisdiction, transaction type, document set and list of comparison fields. Your qualified reviewer defines eligibility, exceptions and the questions the workflow is allowed to prepare.

deliverables.title: An evidence-linked draft report
deliverables.body: A structured draft with document references, pages and excerpts or image crops where appropriate. Proposed matches, discrepancies and unresolved items remain distinct and available for review.

deliverables.title: A controlled review process
deliverables.body: A completeness check before analysis and a qualified review before release. The reviewer can approve, edit or reject findings and retain a record of the decision.

deliverables.title: An evaluation set and operating guide
deliverables.body: Representative historical matters, expected findings and agreed error definitions, followed by documented handling for incomplete files and difficult scans. Acceptance is based on those examples and the scope agreed with your team.

workflow.title: Confirm the matter is eligible
workflow.body: A person selects the relevant documents. The workflow checks whether the required files are present and sufficiently readable for the agreed task.

workflow.title: Extract and compare
workflow.body: Locate the defined facts and compare the agreed sources. Preserve the evidence behind each proposed finding and flag uncertainty.

workflow.title: Review the evidence
workflow.body: The qualified reviewer checks references, resolves discrepancies and records decisions. The draft stays internal while questions remain open.

workflow.title: Approve the output
workflow.body: Prepare the agreed final format or client summary only after approval. Release follows your firm's authorization process.

example.body: A reviewer supplies an approved document package for a defined transaction type. The workflow locates the requested property identifiers and flags an inconsistent description. It provides the relevant pages so the reviewer can decide what the difference means and what to request next.

example.output: A draft comparison table, source-linked findings, a discrepancy list and questions that could not be resolved from the supplied evidence.

faqs.q: Does this work across every U.S. jurisdiction?
faqs.a: Each project starts with a defined jurisdiction and document set. Terminology, records and review requirements vary. Additional jurisdictions are assessed and tested separately with your qualified reviewer before they enter the scope.

faqs.a: The expected behavior is agreed in advance: flag the missing evidence, identify the affected finding and route the matter for review. The workflow should preserve uncertainty where the supplied documents cannot support a conclusion.

faqs.q: Can the system issue a legal opinion or approve a transaction?
faqs.a: Those decisions remain with your professionals. We build document preparation and comparison workflows with defined review gates. Any client-facing summary is checked and authorized through your firm's process.

problems.title: Search context gets rebuilt at every handoff
